decision: Scan source = Drive 'Suzuki Cappucino/Scan Data' (1cBbPLMHVcJ32NoTsjRmxnnzcZJrYnU4L): Full Car + Front Bumper, Front Bumper Lights, Front Bumper Off Hood Open, Rear Bumper, Rear Bumper Trunk Open, Rear End All Removed, Rear End Trunk Open
why: md5 of every STL in the near-duplicate 'Cappuccino/Cappuccino scans' folder matches this one byte-for-byte; this folder also has Rear End Trunk Open. Skipped 'New Turn Signal.stl' (Oct design part, not a capture state), Suzuki_Cappuccino.fbx and the .blends (not our raw scan data / brief: no aftermarket CAD)
Brief: get the gitignored logo from the website; Cloudflare challenge blocks curl's default UA but a browser UA gets the CDN file (6135x1059 RGBA). Same file the ferrari-296 card uses.

decision: One rigid levelling transform for every scan (tools/level.py: RANSAC ground -> +Z, long axis -> Y, nose -Y; /home/user/media/suzuki-cappuccino/level.json); parts cropped with --footprint-from the levelled car
why: Raw Artec frame had ground normal (-0.033,0.042,0.999) and the car's long axis on X. One shared transform keeps every state in the scan frame (huracan-evo tool reused)

decision: All 7 part/state scans registered to the full car as captured - no ICP applied
why: tools/regcheck.py: median part-to-car 1.8-2.7 mm (4 mm car noise floor), ICP would move them <=16 mm (lights, a 50k-tri part) / <=7 mm others. Splat overlays (top/front/side) put every part in its slot. 'Rear Bumper Trunk Open' and 'Rear End Trunk Open' are the same capture (identical counts and distances) - use one

decision: Hood + trunk lid cut from the full car (tools/lids.py: car tris the open-state scan lacks, clipped 85/110 mm inside the body edge = shut lines seen in top-down renders); hinges fitted to the captured open lids (tools/hinge.py): hood axis X at y=-0.392 z=0.776 m (prepped), -52 deg; trunk y=1.104 z=0.845, +63 deg; median 13/12 mm
why: Both open-state scans captured only slivers of the propped lids (9k / 30k tris) - not enough to show as panels, but enough to fit the real hinge. Side-view splat (chk/side_lids.png) puts the hinged lid along the captured sliver cowl-to-tip, so the opening motion is the car's own, not a guessed pivot

decision: Exploded base = full car 3 mm - hood - trunk lid - car tris within 6 mm of the front/rear bumper + lamp part scans, + 'Front Bumper Off, Hood Open' and 'Rear End All Removed' tris >6 mm from that (engine bay, radiator, rear panel, exhaust), their propped lids dropped (tools/composite.py). Front bumper part trimmed around the lamp scan so the lamps explode as their own part
why: Lessons: state scans as captured over the trimmed car; splice over the smallest changed zone. Assembled render (base+hood+trunk+bumpers+lamps) vs untouched car from front and rear 3/4 matches (chk.jpg), so the reassembled car reads as the real one
